OPALX does not store beam moments on `PartBunch` or `ParticleContainer`. Code
that needs the bounds, a mean or a spread of a beam asks
`opalx::moments::compute()` for the moment groups it reads, at the point where
it reads them, and gets a `BeamMoments` value back. The value describes the
particles at the time of the call; nothing is cached between calls. The
implementation is in `opalx/src/Moments/`.

This chapter describes the software structure. The definitions of the reported
quantities (population moments, normalized and geometric emittance, rest-frame
temperatures) are in
[Bunch moments and RMS emittance](../user-guide/conventions/index.qmd#bunch-moments-emittance).

## Moment groups and requests {#beam-moment-requests}

A request is a set of `Moment` groups, declared in `Moments/MomentRequest.h`. A
group is computed completely or not at all.

| Group | `BeamMoments` accessors | Pass | Also computes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Bounds` | `minR()`, `maxR()` | first order | |
| `MeanPosition` | `meanR()` | first order | |
| `MeanMomentum` | `meanP()`, `meanGamma()`, `meanGammaZ()`, `meanKineticEnergy()` | first order | |
| `Spread` | `covariance(i, j)`, `rmsR()`, `rmsP()`, `correlationRP()`, `normalizedEmittance()`, `geometricEmittance()`, `stdKineticEnergy()`, `restFrameTemperature()` | second order | `MeanPosition`, `MeanMomentum` |
| `Polarization` | `meanPolarization()`, `rmsPolarization()`, `meanPolarizationMagnitude()` | polarization | |

`count()`, the global number of particles, is always available. A single
`Moment` converts to a `Request`; requests combine with `|` and `|=` and offer
`contains()`, `without()` and `empty()`. `opalx::moments::allMoments` names
every group.

```cpp
#include "Moments/BeamMoments.h"

using opalx::moments::Moment;

const auto m = opalx::moments::compute(*pc, Moment::MeanPosition | Moment::Spread);
const auto halfWidth = k * m.rmsR();
const auto lower     = m.meanR() - halfWidth;  // m.minR() would throw: Bounds not requested
```

## What `compute()` does {#beam-moment-compute}

`compute(containers, request)` takes one container or a span of containers and
computes the requested groups over their union. It first adds the dependencies
(`withDependencies()` in `Moments/MomentComputation.cpp`: `Spread` adds both
means, because the second-order pass is centred on them) and then runs only the
passes these groups need:

| Pass | Runs for | Reads | MPI reduction |
|---|---|---|---|
| first order | `Bounds`, `MeanPosition`, `MeanMomentum` | `R` only for positions or bounds; `P` and the mass only for momenta | sum of 8 doubles ($\mathbf R$, $\mathbf P$, $\gamma$, kinetic energy) if a mean is requested; min of 6 doubles ($\min\mathbf R$, $-\max\mathbf R$) if bounds are requested |
| second order | `Spread` | `R`, `P`, mass | one sum of 25 doubles: the 21 entries of the symmetric 6x6 covariance, the kinetic-energy variance and three rest-frame temperature sums |
| polarization | `Polarization`, if every container has spin | `Pol` | sum of 6 doubles |

Each pass runs one Kokkos reduction per container, joins the containers on the
host and then calls one allreduce per MPI operator, so passing several
containers adds no MPI messages. The second-order pass is centred on the global
means of the first pass. The rest-frame temperature boosts each momentum into
the frame where the mean momentum vanishes; over several containers this boost
is not mass-weighted, so the temperature is meant for one species.

The reductions are chunked: on host backends (Serial, OpenMP) a work item sums
32 contiguous particles, on devices it strides over the particles. A pass sums
the same quantities whatever else was requested, so a mean comes out bitwise the
same whether it was requested alone or together with `Spread`. A `Polarization`
request on a container without spin skips the pass, and `available()` then does
not contain `Polarization`. The call is timed by the IPPL timer
`computeMoments`.

## Requests during a tracking step {#beam-moment-tracker}

Each consumer asks where it needs a value, in the frame the particles are in at
that point. Unless a class is named, the callers are `ParallelTracker` methods.

| Caller | Request | When |
|---|---|---|
| `makeSpaceChargeFrameTransforms()` | `MeanMomentum` of the primary container | every space-charge field update; the [solve frame](../physics/overview/index.qmd#sec.opalt.space-charge-coordinate-system) follows the mean momentum |
| `CartesianDomainUpdater::` `computeBounds()` | `Bounds` of the solved containers | CartesianPIC3D domain update |
| FFT2D5 `scatterContainer()` and `gatherContainer()` | `MeanMomentum` of the container | every FFT2D5 solve, for the boost into the beam frame |
| `forEachElementInBunchFrame()` | `Bounds` per container | element lookup in `computeExternalFields()` and `applyElementApertures()`, only without spatial candidates or with cyclotron sectors |
| outlier box after the second integration stage | `MeanPosition` and `Spread`, plus the output groups due in this step | `BOUNDPDESTROY > 0`, for active nonempty containers |
| `dumpStats()` | the output groups due in this step | steps with stat, phase-space or step-log output |

`ParallelTracker::outputMomentsDue()` returns the output groups of a step. A stat
record needs `StatWriter::requiredMoments(hasSpin)`: every group, with
`Polarization` only for containers with spin. A phase-space dump with HDF5 needs
`H5PartWrapperForPT::requiredMoments`, and the step log needs `MeanMomentum`.
`DataSink::requiredMoments()` unites the writer requests. On steps without
output the request is empty, so such steps compute only what the solver, the
element lookup and the outlier box ask for.

The outlier box adds the output groups to its own request and keeps the result
in `stepMoments`. `momentsOfContainers()` reuses `stepMoments[i]` if its
`available()` contains the output request, and calls `compute()` otherwise. If
the outlier box deletes particles, `stepMoments` is cleared, because those
values describe the particle set before the deletion.

Startup uses the same call. `TrackRun` prints the beam summary with
`PartBunch::printedMoments`. `ParallelTracker` sets the reference pose of a
nonempty container from `MeanPosition | MeanMomentum`, and
`computeInitialBounds()` requests `Bounds` over all containers.
`Probe::doPreCheck()` requests `Bounds`.

## Classes {#beam-moment-classes}

The diagram shows the moment types and the code around them. Green boxes are the
types and the function in `opalx::moments`; blue boxes are the code that
requests or reads moments. The solvers and elements that call `compute()` share
one box, and so do the output writers, which only declare their requests;
[Requests during a tracking step](#beam-moment-tracker) lists the groups each of
them reads. Dashed arrows are call-time dependencies; the filled diamond means
that a `BeamMoments` value holds the `Request` of the groups it contains.
Writers never call `compute()`; `ParallelTracker` passes them the values.

## Adding a consumer or a moment group {#beam-moment-extending}

- **A new consumer** (solver, element, diagnostic) calls
  `opalx::moments::compute(containers, request)` where it needs the value and
  reads only the groups it requested. One value can serve several reads inside
  one function, but it must not be kept across code that changes the
  particles.
- **A writer that the tracker feeds** declares its groups as a static
  `requiredMoments` request and is added to `DataSink::requiredMoments()`. The outlier-box request and the reuse in
  `momentsOfContainers()` then cover it without new tracker code.
- **Several beams at once:** pass all containers in one call. Each pass still
  costs one allreduce per MPI operator.
- **A new moment group:** add a bit to `Moment` (three of the eight bits are
  free) and, if the statistics output reads it, to `allMoments`. Add its
  dependencies to `withDependencies()`, its sums to an existing pass that reads
  the same arrays or to a new pass with its own allreduce, and accessors that
  call `require()`. Callers that do not request the group do not pay for it.
  Extend `TestBeamMoments` with a host reference for the new quantities.

Rules for every caller:

- `compute()` is collective over `ippl::Comm`. Every rank calls it with the same
  containers and request, also ranks without local particles. A condition around
  a call must have the same value on every rank, for example
  `getTotalNum() > 0`, never `getLocalNum() > 0`.
- All containers of one call must be in the same coordinate frame. The result
  is in that frame.
- A value describes the particle set at the time of the call. After particles
  are deleted, emitted or moved, request again.
- An accessor of a group that `available()` does not contain throws
  `OpalException`.
- Degenerate sets give finite values. An empty set gives zero means and spreads,
  and `Bounds` give a zero-size box at the origin. A vanishing spread gives a
  correlation of zero, and `geometricEmittance()` is zero when
  $\langle\gamma\rangle = 1$.

## Tests {#beam-moment-tests}

`unit_tests/Moments/TestBeamMoments.cpp` compares all groups with a host
reference. It also checks:

- the request contract (dependencies and throwing accessors);
- that the writer requests match what `compute()` provides;
- that shared sums do not depend on the request;
- the kinetic energy with a reference mass and with per-particle masses;
- empty containers, a single particle and zero extent;
- several containers against one concatenated container;
- polarization only when every container has spin;
- the rest-frame temperature of a boosted anisotropic set.

CTest runs the test on one rank. Run the multi-rank cases by hand, for example
from the source directory with the `build_serial` tree of
[Build, Test, and CI](build-test-ci.qmd):

```bash
mpirun -np 2 build_serial/unit_tests/Moments/TestBeamMoments
mpirun -np 4 build_serial/unit_tests/Moments/TestBeamMoments
```
